rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO): annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement:
Rent in RSO units may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD. The rate was 3% for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.

From February 2, 2026:
- Landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities.
- The extra 10% for an added dependent is no longer permitted.
- A 10% increase for an additional non-dependent tenant is still allowed if the landlord acts within 60 days of learning of that tenant.

Increases above the allowable percentage need LAHD approval: capital improvement, primary renovation, seismic retrofit, rehabilitation, or a just and reasonable rent increase.

Rent may be reset to market after:
- a voluntary move-out;
- an eviction for nonpayment or lease violation;
- an eviction for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan;
- an eviction per a City Attorney order;
- a Tenant Buyout Agreement.

Surcharges and pass-throughs:
- Registration fee pass-through of $1.61/month.
- SCEP fee pass-through of $2.83/month.
- Both may be collected only after the landlord registers the units and gives written notice.
- A $3.00 smoke detector surcharge is allowed.

Rent increases were prohibited from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024. State law requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO: just-cause eviction, notice filing and no-fault relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
RSO tenancies may be terminated only for listed causes.
- At-fault causes: nonpayment, uncured lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar agreement, denial of reasonable access, unapproved subtenant.
- No-fault causes: owner or relative move-in, resident manager (only if required by law, an affordable housing covenant or a regulatory agreement), demolition or removal from rental use (Ellis Act, LAMC 151.22-151.28), government order to vacate, HUD sale, residential hotel conversion, conversion to affordable housing.

Nonpayment evictions are barred unless the tenant owes more than the Fair Market Rent for the unit size (from March 27, 2023).

Notice filing: every termination notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.

No-fault evictions:
- The landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice. Failing to file makes the eviction a violation.
- The landlord must give 30-day and 60-day written notice; some evictions require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension.
- The landlord must pay relocation assistance per unit, split pro rata among tenants, at the higher amount if more than one applies.
- Payment must be made available within 15 days of service of the notice, or placed in escrow within that period.
- Reduced 'Mom and Pop' amounts apply only to owner or relative occupancy evictions, and only if: the building has four or fewer units; the landlord has not used the provision in the prior three years; the landlord owns no more than four units plus a single-family home on a separate lot in the City; and the relative owns no residential property in the City.
- Accumulated rent may be offset against relocation, except for government vacate orders or unpermitted dwellings.

Right to Counsel notice: from August 20, 2025 it must be posted, given at the start of the tenancy, and attached to any eviction notice or rental subsidy termination.

Payment within 15 days of notice. Notice copy filed with LAHD within 3 business days. 30/60-day notice (some 120 days or 1-year extension). Owner/relative/manager occupancy filing fee $75.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement:
For covered non-RSO tenancies, landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
- At-fault causes: nonpayment, failure to cure a lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar agreement, denial of reasonable access, unapproved subtenant. At-fault evictions carry no relocation.
- No-fault causes: owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager (only when required by law, an affordable housing covenant or a regulatory agreement), demolition, removal from the market or conversion to non-residential use, government vacate order, HUD sale, residential hotel conversion or demolition, conversion to affordable housing.

No-fault evictions:
- The landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice.
- Relocation is paid at the same Chart A amounts as the RSO, made available within 15 days of service of the notice or placed in escrow within that period.
- A single-family dwelling owned by a natural person who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City owes one month's rent, as payment or credit.
- Accumulated rent may be offset against relocation, except for government vacate orders or unpermitted dwellings.

All eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.

Nonpayment evictions are barred unless the tenant owes more than the Fair Market Rent (from March 27, 2023).

Other duties:
- Properties must be registered annually.
- A Notice of Right to Counsel must be posted from August 20, 2025, given at the start of the tenancy and given with any eviction notice.
- A Notice of Renters' Protections is required for tenancies beginning or renewing on or after January 27, 2023.

The JCO does not regulate rent increases.

rules.title: Los Angeles relocation assistance for demolition or conversion (LAMC 47.06 and 47.07)
rules.requirement: A landlord who demolishes a property, or converts it to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels or commercial uses, must pay relocation assistance whether or not the property is subject to the RSO or JCO. If the City has approved a tentative parcel or tract map for a condominium conversion, the tenant may elect to relocate without receiving a termination notice, and the landlord must still pay relocation assistance.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest
rules.requirement:
Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits.
- Interest accrues monthly from November 1, 1990.
- It is paid monthly or yearly, either as a direct payment or as a credit against rent.
- The landlord chooses the method and must notify the tenant in writing.
- The City sets the rate annually.
- Waiting until the end of the tenancy to pay accumulated interest does not comply.
